bugs.error_message: PR #164 CI failed: cargo-deny 'error[vulnerability]: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries' (RUSTSEC-2026-0285) and Security Vulnerability Scan (cargo audit) exit 1 on the same advisory
bugs.root_cause: Cargo.lock pinned rustls v0.23.44 (transitive: kube client -> hyper-rustls -> rustls), which is below the RUSTSEC-2026-0285 / GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc fix version 0.23.45
bugs.fix: cargo update -p rustls (0.23.44 -> 0.23.45, lockfile-only); verified with `cargo deny check advisories` -> ok; changelog entry added

bugs.error_message: Dependabot PRs #173/#174 failed all CodeQL jobs: "Loaded a configuration file for version '4.38.1', but running version '4.38.0'"
bugs.root_cause: codeql-action monorepo sub-actions (init/analyze/upload-sarif) are distinct dependency names; the dependabot.yml group pattern 'github/codeql-action' matched none of them, so the family split into three PRs and any single bump mismatches init vs analyze
bugs.fix: re-pinned all six github/codeql-action/* refs to v4.38.1 (1c5b675) in one change across codeql/sast/scorecard/build workflows; added 'github/codeql-action/*' to the actions-routine group so the family bumps as one PR

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job: setup_file failed at `out=$(patch_annotation ...)` right after the admission policy applied; 'bats warning: Executed 1 instead of expected 5 tests'
bugs.root_cause: bats executes setup_file with errexit; the activation poll's probe patch exits non-zero exactly when the policy starts denying (the success condition), so the awaited denial aborted the file at the assignment
bugs.fix: append `|| true` to the probe assignment (comment marks it load-bearing); all other patch_annotation call sites already use bats `run`

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job round five: setup passes, then tests 1/2 fail the message assertion and tests 4/5 fail their allow assertion; only test 3 passes
bugs.root_cause: patch_annotation interpolated the value into the patch JSON unescaped; JSON-shaped values like {"namespace":"x"} broke the patch document, so kubectl exited non-zero with a PARSE error before any request — deny tests saw the wrong message, allow tests saw a failure; quote-free values (probe-N, deadbeef) worked, masking it in setup and test 3
bugs.fix: escape embedded quotes in the value (${value//\"/\\\"}) before building the -p document; verified unescaped form fails json.load and escaped form round-trips

bugs.error_message: ScheduledCapacity controller re-patched its own status on every reconcile, re-triggering its own watch: ~50 resourceVersion bumps/sec and a single handback timeout counted 100 times in the Prometheus counter.
bugs.root_cause: Three compounding mistakes in patch_status. (1) Condition::new() stamps lastTransitionTime with Utc::now(), so the computed condition set never equalled the stored one and every reconcile wrote. (2) There was no no-op guard comparing the computed status against the stored one before patching. (3) record_decision_metrics incremented the handback-timeout counter once per reconcile instead of once per transition into the phase. A later rewrite then introduced a fourth: build_status_value silently dropped the targetRef and spotSchedule keys, so the new no-op guard compared a desired status that could never equal the stored one and was permanently disabled, with no test failure and no visible symptom.
bugs.fix: merge_condition_timestamps() preserves each condition's lastTransitionTime unless its `status` actually changed (matched by type, not position); spot_schedule_transition_time() does the same for the mirrored provider timestamp. patch_status() deserialises the computed status into ScheduledCapacityStatus and returns early when it equals the stored one. record_decision_metrics() gates on entered_phase(). build_status_value() always emits every key the controller owns, using explicit JSON null for cleared fields (an omitted key in a merge patch leaves the stored value, so handbackDeadline could never be cleared). Guarded by test_build_status_value_emits_every_field_of_the_status_type, which derives the expected key set from a fully-populated ScheduledCapacityStatus rather than a hand-written list.
bugs.lesson: A controller that logs nothing on a successful reconcile cannot be debugged: the missing-success-log made a working watch look dead and sent the first diagnosis in the wrong direction. Always log reconcile completion. And any status field built by hand must be checked against the type, not against memory.
